correctness.rationale: The cubic product A(q)=1/(f1(q)f2(q)) and exact even-size marking C(q)=4L(q²)A(q) are verified by two independent integer algorithms. Exact eta and E2 transformations yield A(e^-w)=(w/(sqrt(2)pi))exp(pi²/(4w)-w/8)(1+exponentially small), and 4L(e^-2w)=pi²/(6w²)-1/w+1/6+exponentially small. Positivity of the logarithmic coefficients provides a quantitative minor-arc bound, allowing exponentially accurate Bessel-type saddle extraction. Ratios I0/I2 and I1/I2 have expansions 1+2/z+3/z² and 1+3/(2z), giving the stated coefficient -2/(3pi) of sqrt(n) and constant 1/12-1/pi². A runnable checker verifies 126 coefficients via independent recurrences and Bessel convergence at five indices; finite checks are not taken as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The first public cubic-partition weighted-sum paper derives CES/COS generating functions and studies congruences, not an asymptotic expectation. Mauth covers the unweighted cubic count and Schlosser–Zhou other partition models and parts-count biases. Relevant indexed published findings on ordinary-partition mass differ in color model. The exact three-term cubic even-size mean was not found in the accessible primary literature or published index; a stronger unindexed general theorem remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Cubic partitions naturally have a two-even-color versus one-odd-color mass allocation, and the motivating primary work explicitly studies even- and odd-part sums. This theorem supplies a new, precise answer for the typical even mass, including a negative square-root finite-size bias and its constant term, beyond both the source congruences and unweighted count asymptotics. The correction reveals a strict eventual deviation from the naive two-thirds heuristic and can serve as a baseline for finer mass fluctuations. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite computation.
